questions.question: Which of these is given as an example of a liberal democracy?
questions.explanation: Liberal democracies (Norway, Canada, New Zealand, Germany) feature broad rights, constitutional limits and free elections.

questions.question: What distinguishes a totalitarian regime from an authoritarian one?
options: Totalitarian regimes seek control over all aspects of life
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: Authoritarian regimes restrict political freedoms, while totalitarian regimes seek total control over all aspects of life.

questions.question: In a constitutional monarchy, who holds real political power?
questions.explanation: In a constitutional monarchy (Norway, the UK, Sweden, Japan) the monarch is ceremonial; real power rests with elected officials.

questions.question: What does being a "republic" tell us about how democratic a country is?
options: Nothing on its own — a republic can be democratic or authoritarian
It means the head of state is a monarch
questions.explanation: A republic simply means the head of state is elected; this says nothing about how democratic the country actually is.

questions.question: What characterises a federal system?
options: Power is divided between central and regional governments
All power is concentrated in the central government
questions.explanation: Federal systems divide power between central and regional governments, while unitary systems concentrate power centrally.
